title: Weakest Australia batting lineup in a generation: Tough questions for Aussies after Bangladesh dominates Darwin Test
description: Is this the weakest Australian batting lineup in a generation? Analyse the tough questions facing the Aussies after Bangladesh dominated the Darwin 1st Test.
fullText:
Weakest Australia batting lineup in a generation: Tough questions for Aussies after Bangladesh dominates Darwin Test originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Australia's top order continued to struggle against Bangladesh in Darwin.

Cameron Green survived a near-dismissal off Taskin Ahmed, while others like Jake Weatherald and Marnus Labuschagne flopped again.

Ricky Ponting questioned whether Australia's selectors are avoiding necessary changes despite a prolonged run of poor batting form.

There's a strange kind of theatre to watching a champion cricket side slowly come apart, and that's exactly what's unfolding in Darwin right now.

Australia's batting line-up, so often the backbone of this team's success over the past decade, is looking shakier than it has in years, and Bangladesh, of all sides, are the ones exposing it.

Fortune played a starring role on day three, and nowhere more than in Cameron Green's brush with disaster. Facing Taskin Ahmed in the 31st over, Green pushed hard at a length ball nipping back in, got a thick inside edge, and watched it clip the outer edge of leg stump without dislodging the bails, despite Hawk-Eye confirming a spike as the ball brushed past.

The delivery then raced away to the boundary, leaving Taskin and the wicketkeeper stunned. Green went on to finish unbeaten on 43 off 86 balls, and paired with Alex Carey's gritty 19, helped trim the deficit to 67 as Australia limped to 4-161 at stumps. But this was a reprieve, not a recovery, and the Baggy Green dressing room should know it better than anyone.

Hit the stumps... boundary! Is this the luckiest four ever from Cam Green?#PlayoftheDay | @NRMAInsurance | #AUSvBANpic.twitter.com/OprD4iBcCL

Whereas Jake Weatherald's struggles were painfully visible again, as he chopped on for a third-ball duck in Hasan Mahmud's opening over. For a player still finding his feet after debuting during the Ashes, these repeated failures against fiery pace bowling raise questions about whether he's ready for this level just yet.

Across his last 11 innings, he's only avoided single figures on three occasions, numbers that would worry any batting coach, let alone one dealing with conditions Steve Smith himself has called the toughest he's seen in his career.

Marnus Labuschagne's struggles are, if anything, more concerning simply because they've dragged on far longer. He showed some fight early on, absorbing a couple of blows to the pads, before inexplicably missing a full delivery from Taijul Islam that drifted past his defences entirely unchallenged.

Before this outing, he has been dismissed for single digits in half of his last 32 Test innings. It is a stat that should set off alarm bells in any selection meeting, regardless of reputation or past achievements.

MORE: 'Frailties in technique': Ponting slams Australia's top order following collapse in 1st Test vs Bangladesh

While the headlines have understandably gone to Weatherald and Labuschagne, Green cannot escape criticism despite showing grit in the second innings with a well-made, patient 104, with just four boundaries and one six in the innings.

Since that breakthrough unbeaten 174 in Wellington back in March 2024, he's averaging just under 23 (before the second innings knock), numbers that don't match the promise he showed in that innings, or the responsibility he's since been handed in the middle order.

Add Beau Webster into that same conversation, and Australia suddenly have three or four players in the top six whose places would ordinarily be under threat, rather than protected by reputation alone.

Both batsmen have looked desperately for control. Their lack of footwork, the tendency to nick on balls at the line of uncertainty, and the propensity to throw away wickets through reckless shot selection are major causes of worry.

Although Smith has come out swinging in defence of his colleagues and blamed the conditions, the technical faults have been too glaring.

"I've said for a while that batting at the top of the order in Australia at the moment is as tough as I've seen in my career - by a mile," he said.

"The ball's seaming significantly. It's extremely tricky and you need some luck definitely as a top-order batter. The guys got off to a decent start today … and then we obviously lost a few in clumps there."

MORE: Cricket World reacts as Bangladesh dominate Australia on Day 2 in Darwin Test

Former Australian captain Ricky Ponting cut through the excuses when he was dissecting the batting collapse.

"You know, we're not asking guys to go out and get 100 or 200 out there, but we need our top order to find a way," he said, before turning his attention to the technical side of things. "Once again, I think we saw the frailties in technique with this top order."

He went further, noting that the batting group has had a full year to sort itself out and yet things have not improved. Ponting feels that the Australian selectors should look at fresh faces instead of sticking with the dead wood who have failed to produce the goods over an extended period of time.

"It has been at least 12 months where they have had the opportunity to make changes, especially with the batting group," he said on SEN's Fireball.

"Go with a bit of gut feel and pick on talent because what we've got in the current side now, and it has been for a couple of years, has not looked up to the mark of Test cricket. It (change) is going to happen.

"They've got 21 Tests coming up until the end of the World Test Championship (WTC). They're at home to New Zealand, they're away to South Africa, they're away to India. Inevitably, they'll be going through 16-18 players in this next little run. So I think organically it will start to happen where guys will be coming in and out just to try and manage them through until the end of it."

MORE: Full list of Bangladesh batters to score century in Australia: Tanizd creates history

Ponting's right, and the numbers back him up completely. Labuschagne's pattern of dismissals isn't a rough patch anymore. It's simply who he is right now as a batter, and reputation shouldn't keep shielding him from consequences that any other player would face.

The same logic applies to Green and Weatherald: talent got them into this side, but talent alone doesn't earn indefinite chances when the returns keep coming up short series after series. What's genuinely alarming here isn't one bad session against Bangladesh; it's that this exact conversation has been happening for over a year without any real action following it.

Australia have a brutal 12 months ahead, including South Africa and India, and turning up to those tours with unresolved batting problems would be close to reckless. If the second innings on a flat Darwin pitch doesn't produce answers, selectors need the nerve to finally make the calls Ponting's clearly hinting they've been avoiding for too long.

title: Louis Foster Just Got Pole at Markham
description: After what seemed to be a disastrous day yesterday, the NTT IndyCar Series took to the streets of Markham, Ontario, for the first time today. fullText:
After what seemed to be a disastrous day yesterday, the NTT IndyCar Series took to the streets of Markham, Ontario, for the first time today. Today's schedule saw both practices and qualifying, in preparation for tomorrows inaugural race.

One driver in particular found his sweet spot on this track: RLL's Louis Foster. Sister consistently remained in the top three throughout both practice sessions. In the first practice session, Foster placed third, trailing behind AJ Foyt rookie Caio Collet and Chip Ganassi champion Alex Palou. He trailed Collet by less than a tenth of a second, and Palou by a tenth.

In the second practice session, Foster came first with a time of 1:14:1793, followed by Marcus Ericsson, who had a lap time of 1:14:1933. David Malukas, Kyle Kirkwood, and Mick Schumacher rounded out the top five.

During the second session, Palou struggled with the course, ending up in seventh. He'd continue to struggle into qualifying, where he ended up in 12th.

Foster came just behind Malukas in the first round of qualifying. Dumbbell qualifying is divided into two groups, he did not qualify in the same group as Palou. Palou qualified first in group one.

In the second round, the pressure was on for drivers to make the Fast Six. The top six in both groups made the second round. Ericsson, Scott McLaughlin, rookie Dennis Hauger, Rinus Veekay, Christian Lundgaard, and Foster secured the spots and made the Fast Six.

All lap times were within a second of each other. Foster secured pole position with a lap time of 1:13:2383, getting his second-ever pole position in the series.  Lundgaard secured second place, just about four-tenths behind Foster. Behind this front row is McLaughlin and Ericsson in the second row, and Hauger and Veeka in the third row.

The streets of Markham will be open for full-fledged chaos at the green flag. The green flag waives at 12 p.m. EST, live on FOX.

fullText:
Few things are certain in sport. But for now, it seems like San Diego FC making life difficult for LAFC is one of them.

The Chrome-and-Azul earned a hard-fought 1-0 win over their Southern California foes, grabbing all three points at BMO Stadium for the second straight season and improving their all-time MLS record vs. the Black & Gold to 3W-0L-1D.

Saturday's dramatic result came vía an 89th-minute penalty-kick winner from Anders Dreyer.

"I'm just focused on a really complete performance against a top team," head coach Mikey Varas said postgame.

"This is high-level football at its best. You go away to LA with all the firepower they have, and you're going to concede chances. You're going to concede momentum at times."

After setting a nearly impossibly high bar during a historic 2025 MLS expansion season, San Diego have experienced plenty of ups and downs in year two.

Entering Saturday's meeting with LAFC, the expectation was that LAFC – riding an eight-game unbeaten run across all competitions dating back to before the 2026 FIFA World Cup break – would take care of business at home.

That's not how it went. San Diego contained LAFC's superstar duo of Son Heung-Min and Denis Bouanga, and when the visitors were awarded a late penalty following Video Review, Dreyer got the job done.

The 2025 MLS Newcomer of the Year now has 2g/4a in four all-time meetings against LAFC.

Defensively, goalkeeper CJ Dos Santos stepped up with three huge saves. The Philadelphia native, fresh off a World Cup trip as Cape Verde's backup goalkeeper, has been a revelation in recent weeks, starting every game since the league's return to play.

"It's all about taking it one day at a time, one game at a time, one training session at a time, one rep at a time," Dos Santos said. "That's the most important thing. We don't want to get too far ahead of ourselves.

"We know what our objectives are, we know what our goals are, and we're going to do everything possible to make them come true."

Saturday's win has bigger implications for San Diego than bragging rights over arguably California's most stacked roster.

It brings them within one point of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs and could give them the confidence to push on towards a postseason return after reaching last year's Western Conference Final.

With new Designated Player winger Elias Achouri also coming off the bench to make his debut, the tide certainly seems to be turning for San Diego - even with Dreyer's late sending off for a second yellow card.

"This is a game where you could see that everybody was committed to doing the dirty work and making sure we did whatever was possible to win the game, while still looking like us," Varas said.

"It's absolutely a game we can build on and use as inspiration to recognize what we can do, because we know we can still take steps forward as well."

title: Lakers have massive problem with $50M three-time NBA champion despite trading for Walker Kessler
description: The Los Angeles Lakers have made some moves this offseason. However, with the moves made, it seems they still have a big issue heading into the season.
fullText:
Lakers have massive problem with $50M three-time NBA champion despite trading for Walker Kessler originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Los Angeles Lakers have made several major moves this offseason to set themselves up for the near future. Los Angeles made three moves in free agency right away, significantly changing the outlook of the organization.

As soon as the new league year began, the Lakers made a blockbuster move by trading for Utah Jazz big man Walker Kessler.

"The Los Angeles Lakers started the process of remaking their roster in the wake of LeBron James' decision to leave with a blockbuster trade and a trio of free agency signings Wednesday. Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Lakers are acquiring Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz for unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and first-round swaps in 2028 and 2030," ESPN wrote.

Not long after, Los Angeles traded last season's starting center, Deandre Ayton, to the Washington Wizards. The Lakers then signed veteran center Kevon Looney.

"While the Los Angeles Lakers continue to actively pursue unrestricted free agent wing Jonathan Kuminga, league sources told ESPN on Tuesday, they've agreed to a one-year deal with veteran center Kevon Looney, who was Kuminga's teammate while with the Golden State Warriors. The deal is worth $3.9 million," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote.

Signing Looney was a gamble in itself, as the three-time NBA champion is no longer the player he once was. The Lakers have not been able to add another true backup center, meaning Looney is expected to fill that role. Lake Show Life's Tyler Watts believes that could be a major problem for Los Angeles.

"This signing was a gamble. Loon was a replacement-level player last season. The Lakers clearly believe he will be better, but they need another option. Going into the season with just two true centers is a problem. If Kessler is forced to miss time, the Lakers have serious issues on defense and at the five," Watts wrote.

The Lakers need to find a better backup center, and they know it. However, the team does not have many attractive trade pieces to acquire one. Looney was once a valuable big man for the Golden State Warriors, but he is no longer the same player he was during his prime.

Looney has made $50 million throughout his career. Los Angeles loves having Kessler as its starting center, but he does have an injury history. At this point, relying on Kessler as the primary starter without a reliable backup is not a position the Lakers want to find themselves in.

title: Lima Grand Prix 2026: Breakthrough victories on Day Two

fullText:

International Judo Federation Gender Equality & Development Commission Member Mrs Katiuska SANTAELLA awarded the medals.

International Judo Federation International Relations Commission Director Mr Oscar CASSINERIO awarded the medals.

Lima is a beautiful city with beautiful people. The atmosphere is very nice and see you next time in Lima.

I didn't think I was winning today, to be honest, because we did some hard training before but I think in the end we kind of managed to do it, the training, and I'm like, I don't know what to say… Amazing.

title: Mackenzie Dern fails to step out of Weili Zhang’s shadow with ho-hum UFC 330 win
description: Based on how hard Dana White and the gang have been pushing Mackenzie Dern, you know they were hoping her UFC 330 fight against Gillian Robertson would be a star-making affair. Alas, like most best laid plans in MMA, that didn’t quite come together. Instead, Dern struggled to submit her opponent despite ample time on […]
fullText:
Based on how hard Dana White and the gang have been pushing Mackenzie Dern, you know they were hoping her UFC 330 fight against Gillian Robertson would be a star-making affair.

Alas, like most best laid plans in MMA, that didn't quite come together. Instead, Dern struggled to submit her opponent despite ample time on the canvas, and a fight that started out as a fun brawl slowly ground down to a complete stall by round five.

Dern took the fight convincingly with 49–46, 49–46, and 48–47 scores, and Robertson never really had anything for the champion across five rounds. Mackenzie was faster with her striking, hit harder, kicked harder, and was definitely levels above Robertson when things hit the mat. She almost secured a rear naked choke in the dying seconds of the first round, but Robertson's grit allowed her to hold on until the buzzer.

¡Dominante actuación de la brasileña! 🇧🇷

Así fue como Mackenzie Dern pasó por encima de Gillian Robertson en Philadelphia. 🔥 ¡Obra de arte! 

🔴 #UFC330 EN VIVO por Paramount + pic.twitter.com/jGDwvS15dy

That was as exciting as the fight got. Dern hit several takedowns from there and was able to control Robertson on the ground, but she never threatened another finish. Round five saw her stuck on her back for multiple minutes. She won, and was never in danger of losing, But it just wasn't the kind of bout that makes fans clamor to see more.

It certainly doesn't erase the perception amongst more tuned-in fight fans that Dern is merely a placeholder champion until Weili Zhang returns to the division. Zhang relinquished the strawweight in October 2025 as part of a move to women's flyweight, only to suffer a horribly one-sided loss to Valentina Shevchenko a month later.

It's been nine months since then and we haven't heard a fight-related peep from Zhang since. Will she even return, let alone back at strawweight? If she does, the general consensus is she'd whup Mackenzie Dern's butt across the octagon with ease. Dern's performance tonight against Robertson will only entrench that opinion further.

Tonight in Philadelphia, she had her chance to step out from the shadow of Weili Zhang with a powerful performance. What we saw didn't qualify.

title: Rafael Jódar Explains Himself to Denis Shapovalov After Drama Erupts During Their Cincinnati Open Clash
description: Rafael Jódar and Denis Shapovalov’s Cincinnati Open clash not only delivered a riveting battle on the court but also sparked controversy when the Canadian voiced his frustration with Jódar’s actions. Following the match, the two players engaged in conversation as they appeared to address the incident.
fullText:
Rafael Jódar and Denis Shapovalov's Cincinnati Open clash not only delivered a riveting battle on the court but also sparked controversy when the Canadian voiced his frustration with Jódar's actions. Following the match, the two players engaged in conversation as they appeared to address the incident.

Following a first-round bye, No. 12 seed Jódar engaged in a closely contested battle with Shapovalov in the second round of the Cincinnati Open. The Spaniard won the opening set, while Shapovalov fought back to take the second set to force a decider that was filled with drama.

With the Canadian leading 2-1 in the decider, Jódar called for a medical timeout and received treatment on his left leg. The Spaniard required another pause in play while trailing 1-4 after his shoelaces broke.

Jódar then found himself on the brink of defeat as Shapovalov took a 5-1 lead. However, the 19-year-old saved two match points and started mounting an incredible comeback. The drama continued when Jódar's shoelaces broke for the second time while he was trailing 3-5, forcing another stoppage to change shoes.

Shapovalov appeared frustrated by the situation, complaining that the Spaniard used his previous break not only to change shoes but also to drink water.

"Shapovalov, he's even saying to Jódar that the last time he changed shoes, he was also getting water," the commentator said.

Jódar went on to complete a remarkable comeback, winning six games in a row to secure a 7-5, 4-6, 7-5 victory. When Shapovalov approached him for the post-match handshake, the 19-year-old appeared to explain the situation with the shoelaces, as noted by the commentator.

"Jódar I think just explaining the situation with regards to the laces," the commentator said.

This is not the first time Jódar has had trouble with his shoelaces, as he also had to stop play to deal with the issue during his matches at the Mubadala DC Open and the Canadian Open.

MORE: 'Looks Like It Hurts' – Eugenie Bouchard Stunned As Coco Gauff, Rafael Jódar Hit Themselves With Rackets at Canadian Open

Up next, Rafael Jódar will lock horns with No. 22 seed Alejandro Tabilo in the third round of the Cincinnati Open. A win would send the Spaniard into the fourth round, where he will take on either Flavio Cobolli or Alexander Blockx.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Barcelona ready to fly top defensive target early next week as summer transfer nears – Romano
description: Barcelona could be only days away from bringing Joao Cancelo back to the club for a third spell, with the Portuguese defender working towards an exit from Al Hilal.According to transfer expert Fabrizi...
fullText:
Barcelona could be only days away from bringing Joao Cancelo back to the club for a third spell, with the Portuguese defender working towards an exit from Al Hilal.

According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Barcelona are prepared to fly Cancelo to the city early next week once Al Hilal give the final approval for his departure.

The Blaugrana are increasingly confident that the situation will be resolved soon, with the player himself pushing to complete his return.

The Barcelona transfer news regarding the defender suggests that Cancelo's future could be settled through the termination of his contract with the Saudi Pro League side.

Discussions involving the player, his representatives and Al Hilal are understood to be ongoing as all parties attempt to find a solution.

The financial side of the Joao Cancelo transfer has been one of the main issues during negotiations.

Cancelo has no place in Simone Inzaghi's squad. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Barcelona and Al Hilal had reportedly appeared to be moving towards a deal worth around €10 million.

However, the Saudi side then raised their asking price to €15 million, creating fresh uncertainty over how the transfer would be completed.

That situation now appears to have opened the door to another route, and Barcelona are ready to act if the Saudi club formally clears the way.

Internally, the Catalan giants are hopeful of completing the necessary paperwork and bringing the Portuguese international back to Barcelona within the coming days.

As far as Cancelo is concerned, the defender's position at the Saudi club has also strengthened Barcelona's belief that a solution can be found.

Notably, he was left out of Al Hilal's matchday squad for their opening league fixture, while Simone Inzaghi has indicated that the player's future is ultimately a matter for the club to resolve.

Cancelo is close to returning to Barcelona. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

This would mark Cancelo's third chapter at Barcelona after his earlier spell and his loan return during the second half of the 2025-26 campaign.

His latest stint gave Hansi Flick another experienced option across both full-back positions, with the Barcelona coach previously highlighting the Portuguese player's quality and attacking strength.

There will always be questions about Cancelo's defensive consistency, particularly against the strongest opposition. However, his technical ability and versatility give Barcelona something different.

A player capable of operating on both sides of the defence can be especially useful over a long season, particularly for a squad competing across several competitions.

For Hansi Flick, Cancelo would not be an unknown signing requiring months to settle, as he already knows the environment, and his previous spell showed that he can provide an attacking threat from deep positions.

If Barcelona can complete the deal on favourable terms, Cancelo's return could prove to be a sensible piece of business rather than a risky transfer gamble.

fullText:

Tresean Gore got his teeth knocked out 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/URotL5IrNC

The 32-year-old is now riding the second two-fight winning streak of his UFC career. Before defeating Luque, Gore pulled off a massive upset earlier this year when he put Azamat Bekoev to sleep.

Gore is now 4-4 inside the Octagon and hopes his latest victory will earn him a fight against someone close to the Middleweight rankings.

At this time, Gore's scan results have not been publicly disclosed. However, given the damage to his mouth, do not be surprised if some gnarly dental images surface in the coming days.

title: Just in: Real Madrid youth team forward leaves Spain to sign three-year contract in Libya
description: Real Madrid Castilla forward Loren Zuniga has brought his time at the club to an end, with the young striker set to continue his career in Libya, reports Mundo Deportivo.Zuniga has joined Al Madina, s...
fullText:
Real Madrid Castilla forward Loren Zuniga has brought his time at the club to an end, with the young striker set to continue his career in Libya, reports Mundo Deportivo.

Zuniga has joined Al Madina, signing a three-year contract with the Tripoli-based club after completing a three-year spell in Real Madrid's youth setup.

The move marks a major change for the forward, who arrived at La Fabrica in 2023 from Malaga and went on to progress through the club's academy before earning his chance with Castilla last season.

During his time with Real Madrid Castilla, Zuniga scored six goals and gained valuable experience at senior level.

However, his next step will now take him away from Spanish football as he begins a new chapter in the Libyan league.

Zuniga joined Real Madrid with the aim of continuing his development within one of the most competitive youth systems in European football.

After arriving from Malaga in 2023, the forward spent the next few years working his way through La Fabrica.

His progress eventually led to a place in the Castilla squad, where he was able to show his qualities at a higher level.

Last season proved to be an important one for the striker, as his six goals for Castilla helped him gain further attention and also played a role in his growing profile beyond club football.

The Real Madrid academy graduate's performances were rewarded with an international opportunity as well.

Zuniga earned a call-up to the Equatorial Guinea national team and was included in the squad for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Representing Equatorial Guinea at the tournament added another important milestone to his career and showed how his development at club level had helped open doors on the international stage.

Now, though, the forward's Real Madrid journey has come to a close.

Zuniga's next destination is Al Madina, with the Libyan side handing him a contract that will keep him at the club for the next three seasons.

Based in Tripoli, Al Madina have been active in the Spanish market, and Zuniga is not the only player with links to Spanish football to arrive recently.

Notably, the club have also brought in Abde Damar on loan from Zamora.

For Zuniga, he leaves with senior experience at Castilla, six goals from last season and an Africa Cup of Nations appearance on his record.

title: Skip Bayless uses Caitlyn Jenner’s take to justify a trans athletes ban in the WNBA
description: Media personality Skip Bayless has supported the ban on trans athletes in the WNBA by citing Caitlyn Jenner as an example. Caitlyn Jenner won the 1976 Olympic gold medal in the decathlon as Bruce Jenner before transitioning to a woman and becoming one of the most high-profile trans people in the world.
fullText:
Media personality Skip Bayless has supported the ban on trans athletes in the WNBA by citing Caitlyn Jenner as an example.

Caitlyn Jenner won the 1976 Olympic gold medal in the decathlon as Bruce Jenner before transitioning to a woman and becoming one of the most high-profile trans people in the world.

However, Jenner also supports the view that trans women athletes shouldn't participate in women's sports, something that Skip Bayless believes is pertinent to the recent WNBA debate.

Bayless shared his point of view on X, urging the WNBA to listen to Jenner as a living example of a biological male athlete who completed the transition to being a trans woman.

"Caitlyn Jenner, as Bruce Jenner, won gold in the Olympic decathlon. Caitlyn Jenner now says biological boys/men should NOT be allowed to compete against girls/women: "We have to protect women's sports." Listening, WNBA?"

The WNBA doesn't have a trans athlete prospect to consider, or has ever had one in its 30-year history, so the recent debate over the subject has polarised the league's fanbase unnecessarily.

This also led to former NBA players Enes Kanter and Royce White declaring for the WNBA Draft to make the imagined problem into reality.

The WNBA is standing firm that they will not change their eligibility criteria because of 'bad-faith actors,' but they will likely have to release a nuanced eligibility criteria to avoid blanket banning trans athletes while protecting biological women in the WNBA.

Jenner recently went on Fox to discuss Kanter and White declaring for the WNBA Draft, supporting their action in a way to point out the WNBA's hypocrisy and advocating for a ban on trans athletes.

"Yes, they are. Enes is the other one that's out there. He's been doing the same thing. They're showing the hypocrisy of what's going on out there in the WNBA… XX, you're in; XY, you're out. It's that simple. We have to protect women's sports."

Jenner has been very outspoken in recent years against trans women competing against biological women, which many consider a blow to trans athletes, as one of their biggest potential advocates is one of their biggest detractors.

title: Match review: Royals break single-season win record against Bay FC, Real Salt Lake draws with Minnesota
description: Double header at America First Field ends in victory for Royals and a stalemate for the Claret-and-Cobalt.
fullText:
Utah Royals FC opened up a doubleheader weekend for professional soccer in Utah at America First Field with a 3-2 victory over Bay FC Friday evening in front of 7,020 fans, continuing its unbeaten streak against the visiting Northern California side in its sixth head-to-head matchup for the 2024 expansion partners.

Real Salt Lake battled to a 1-1 stalemate in front of 20,119 fans against Minnesota United FC Saturday night, both sides finding the net late in the second half. The match was RSL's fourth consecutive at home over a congested month of August, with two wins and two draws heading into Wednesday's contest against Dallas.

After conceding in the sixth minute, the Royals responded with lightning-fast efficiency, as Japanese defender Miyabi Moriya netted the equalizer a minute and three seconds later to her first goal as a Royal and first NWSL goal since Nov. 2, 2025.

A 24th-minute goal by Narumi Miura, assisted by forward Cloé Lacasse, earned the Canadian her eighth assist of 2026, tied for second-most in the NWSL with Portland Thorns forward Pietra Tordin.

In the 81st minute, URFC midfielder and Utah native Courtney Brown entered the match, hitting a milestone with her 50th NWSL appearance.

The 79th-minute game-winning penalty conversion by Japanese forward Mina Tanaka helped lift the Royals to yet another Club record, winning 11 games on the year — the most in a single season. With all three of Utah's goal scorers having Japanese citizenship, the trio became the first ever to do so in the same game in NWSL history.

In Saturday evening's match, Columbian defender Juan Jose Arias made his first MLS start with poise and energy following multiple Leagues Cup starts.

To begin, the match was mainly a defensive battle highlighted by RSL defender Lukas Engel. RSL Captain and goalkeeper Rafael Cabral found himself out of position as a header made its way toward the open net, but the Dane came up big, racing to make a goal-line clearance in the 34th minute.

RSL's 2026 Golden Boot leader, Sergi Solans, ultimately gave the home side the lead in the 82nd minute assisted by star midfielder Diego Luna. The Spanish rookie netted his fourth goal in five matches throughout the month of August, and his 12th goal across all competitions in 2026 (eighth in MLS).

With the visitors finding the late equalizer, the Claret-and-Cobalt drop to a 10-1-2 record in its home fortress at America First Field.

"Having three Japanese players score a goal is something incredibly special, I'd say," URFC head coach Jimmy Coenraets said. "You can see the chemistry between them. So there is so much to be proud of tonight."

"We were creating those chances all night, and if we bury them, it could easily have been a 3-0 or 4-0 game like the last two games," RSL head coach Pablo Mastroeni said. "We didn't capitalize and we gave up an easy goal and it's a 1-1 game, but is the performance bad? No, not at all, and that's what I said to the players. Tonight, we didn't capitalize, and that's the difference."

The Friday night matchup at America First Field was action-packed from the beginning.

Bay FC took the early lead, netting a goal in the sixth minute after a deflected pass out of the box by URFC goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn. Just a little more than a minute later, the home side equalized, quickly bringing the ball up the field and into the opposing penalty box for Miyabi, who tied the score at 1-1 just seven minutes in.

The Royals then took a 2-1 lead in the 24th minute, with a long-range bullet from Japanese midfielder Narumi for her third of the season. However, the visitors soon leveled the score once again, netting a goal off a corner kick in the 29th minute.

After a scoreless second half, the home side regained the lead with a 79th-minute goal from the penalty spot. The score brought Tanaka to six goals in 2026, to go along with four assists. The forward's game-winning goal lifted the home side to a 3-2 victory and brought Utah atop the NWSL for the most goals scored thus far in 2026 at 35, also a team record.

The Claret-and-Cobalt pressured the Minnesota defense early on before Utah native Zach Booth was subbed out of the game in the 13th minute due to injury, Polish midfielder Dominik Marczuk entering in his place.

After a 34th-minute clearance by Engel, the home side was forced to defend four consecutive corners, thwarting consecutive offensive chances for Minnesota to send both sides into the locker room scoreless.

While RSL maintained a high level of possession throughout the first 25 minutes of the second half, the visitors were awarded a free kick just outside the 18-yard box in the 70th minute and Cabral showcased his presence between the posts, making a 1-on-1 save to keep the Loons off the scoresheet.

Real Salt Lake continued the second half with energy.

Continuing to pressure the visitors' defense to find tangible offensive opportunities, Solans nearly gave the home side the lead in the 66th minute, his shot going just right of the goal. The fight from the RSL side finally paid off with an 82nd-minute goal by Solans to give his team the late 1-0 lead.

Just five minutes later, Minnesota found the equalizer, snapping RSL's 353-minute shutout streak. The draw on Saturday night now extends RSL to a five-match winless streak.

Real Salt Lake remains in Utah for its final of five consecutive home matches for a mid-week matchup against Dallas FC on Wednesday. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. and tickets for the match can be purchased at RSL.com.

Utah Royals FC head to the west coast on Saturday to take on the San Diego Wave. Kickoff for that match is scheduled for 8 p.m. and will be streaming on Amazon Prime Video.

title: UFC 330 takeaways: Islam Makhachev remains king, but Ian Machado Garry leaves with something, too
description: Islam Makhachev held onto his title at UFC 330, but did future challengers get a glimpse of the blueprint to beat him? That and other takeaways from a night of two title fights in Philadelphia.
fullText:
UFC 330 mixed wild upsets with workmanlike title defenses from Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia on Saturday night. Here are the five big takeaways from a night with two title fights and lots of undercard surprises:

1. Islam Makhachev is still the champ, but the aura of invincibility might have a couple new holes in it. In the fifth round of his UFC welterweight title defense, the champ found himself in an unfamiliar situation. Instead of being the guy who could always threaten with a takedown, suddenly he looked like a guy who desperately needed one.

He got it, too. He dragged Ian Machado Garry down for his seventh takedown in 15 attempts. This time he made it count, moving to Garry's back and effectively securing the win with a couple minutes still to go in the final round. But this wasn't the dominant Makhachev we're used to, hauling opponents into his world and then devouring them at his leisure. This time Makhachev seemed content to hold on and run out the clock, which is likely a testament to how hard Garry made him work for this win.

To be fair, the scorecards were just a formality by that point. You could argue that Garry won the third and fourth rounds, but you'd have to stretch the bounds of believability to say anything beyond that. Makhachev led the dance and even dropped him with a head kick in the second, so this was clearly his night.

Still, for the other welterweight contenders out there, a potential blueprint seemed to take shape at certain points. Make this man work. Chop away at his body. Actually stop some takedowns as the fight wears on. Then do just a little bit extra when he's catching his breath. All easier said than done. But here, maybe for the first time, it began to seem possible.

2. Garry fought — and lost — like a man who didn't need anyone's help to know who he was. All week long it was the confidence of the challenger that surprised people. Here he was getting ready to step into a cage against the human woodchipper from Dagestan, and he was somehow walking around with his head high and a smile on his face, like it was something he might actually be looking forward to.

Garry has taken a lot of heat from fans, and he's probably still not everyone's cup of Irish breakfast. But any man who can make Makhachev sweat (and swell) like that over five rounds and still hold his head up the same way going out as he did coming in, well, you've got to respect it. Even if you don't come all the way around to liking it.

3. Mackenzie Dern had bursts and flashes where she really looked like a UFC champ. Unfortunately, she couldn't sustain them long enough to put Gillian Robertson away, which really would have helped make her case.

That's not to say that it wasn't a strong overall performance for Dern. She came out in the first and fought with real purpose and confidence, which hasn't always been the case in her UFC tenure. But wearing that strawweight title comes with certain expectations. If Dern wants fans to look at her as something other than a placeholder champ while Weili Zhang is away, she needs that extra bit of emphasis that only a finish can provide. She didn't get it this time, but she did take some steps in the right direction.

4. It was a good night to be a big underdog. Going solely by the oddsmakers, you'd have thought UFC 330 was peppered with major mismatches. Three undercard fights featured fighters who were 8-1 favorites or greater. Prior to the main card, only two bouts had betting odds that seemed anywhere close to even. But apparently someone forgot to tell the underdogs that they had no shot.

It started with the curtain-jerker, as the night's biggest underdog, Jeremiah Wells, overcome 9-1 odds to shock Myktybek Orolbai with a late finish via choke. The venerable Neil Magny followed suit in the very next fight, becoming one of the UFC's winningest underdogs of all time. Dustin Stoltzfus, who was supposed to be a lamb headed to slaughter at +500 on some sportsbooks, reminded us that there's a reason they still bother to have the fights even when everyone thinks the outcome is obvious.

It's a good reminder that, in a sport with so many variables and so many different ways to win (and lose), a true sure thing remains mostly a myth.

5. After more than 15 uninterrupted years in the UFC, Edson Barboza has called it a career. He didn't get a hero's farewell. He didn't even get any particularly friendly matchmaking there at the end. At the dignified age of 40, he had to go in there and take his lumps at the hands of Esteban Ribovics, a man a full decade younger. The result was a fourth consecutive loss and a goodbye that mixed blood and tears.

Incredible career for Edson Barboza. So many memorable moments over the years 👏 pic.twitter.com/4QxNpPBh3b

An emotional Barboza told the Philly crowd that, whatever else he did over the course of 20 years spent in fight sports, he always gave it his best. No one can say he was lying. In his prime, Barboza was a buzzsaw who could shred your thighs and snap off your consciousness. He's the owner of some highlights that the UFC will still be showing years from now. He was never an easy night of work for anyone, even when the years and the miles began to add up. He shared the cage with some greats and he was always worth the price of admission.

This sport isn't great at goodbyes, and it's especially bad at knowing how to show the proper appreciation for those non-champs who gave it everything they had. But if anyone deserves our respect on his way out the door, it's Barboza. If you don't believe it, go ask anyone who's ever been kicked by him.

title: Donald flies Welsh flag in Hundred final at Lord's
description: Welsh Fire might not be in the Hundred final on Sunday at Lord's but Welsh batter Aneurin Donald is looking to take centre stage.
fullText:
Welsh Fire might not be involved in The Hundred final on Sunday at Lord's but there is set to be a Welsh batter.

Aneurin Donald will take his place in the top order of the Nottingham-based Trent Rockets when they face Manchester Superchargers this evening (18:15 BST).

The 29-year-old from Gorseinon near Swansea started his career with Glamorgan but left in 2018 and is now at Derbyshire.

"I am massively proud and passionate of my heritage and Welsh cricket," said Donald.

"I left Glamorgan a long time ago but love to keep a track of Welsh cricket even if I'm doing it with a Trent Rockets shirt on."

And Donald is quick to remind people it is the England and Wales Cricket Board.

"I'm always correcting people that I'm playing as a Welshman, not an Englishman, and it's something I'll always push.

"Glamorgan and Wales have a special place in my heart and there'll always be that attachment to Welsh cricket.

"I'm looking forward to hopefully flying the flag at Lord's and getting a trophy."

Donald is hoping to be part of a successful Trent Rockets side in front of a capacity crowd in London.

"It's going to be exciting to roll out in Lord's in front of a full crowd in a final," he said.

"Lifting a trophy would be a huge moment. For myself and my career, it'd be up there.

"I want to try and soak the day in, because they come and go quickly and careers are short."

Donald was picked up in the auction by Trent Rockets and experienced a successful T20 Blast campaign with Derbyshire.

He was the sixth highest runs scorer with 489 in the 20-overs tournament, but it was his astonishing strike of 230 that stood out.

"It's an obvious strength of mine, and this format [The Hundred] is compressed even more," said Donald.

"It's more important you're efficient with your balls and that's something that seems to have worked over the past few years.

"The format is different for the players, probably more so than people realise because it is so much faster."

After being forced to wait his chance with the Rockets' international line-up, Donald came in for injured England batter Tom Banton and kept up that strike rate when Rockets topped the table.

"I've been fortunate enough to get a chance, which is difficult with these teams," said Donald.

"To be able to have played a small part in this and feel I've finally put my stamp at this level has been important.

"I'm lucky to have landed at Trent Rockets, it's an unbelievable place to be involved.

"It is tough to get in the side and hold a spot down, but when you get a chance you're desperate to take it with both hands.

"As you go up the levels, you've got to take opportunities you get.

"I feel like I've been around the block a bit. I'm probably in the best position to kind of cope with that and be ready for my chance."

Donald knows he is in his position because of his county career.

"I love Derbyshire and it's nice to feel settled, they've been amazing since I moved there," said Donald.

"My game has gone from strength to strength and I've got a lot to thank [director of cricket] Mickey Arthur and the club for.

"I feel so valued. Getting the opportunity to captain in white ball cricket is a massive feather in my cap and something I always wanted to do."

All you need to know about the 2026 Hundred finals

The Hundred 2026 tables, top run-scorers & wicket-takers

Donald was a Glamorgan prodigy who seemed destined for senior international honours when playing for England Under-19s.

That never quite materialised, but a decade on Donald has not given up hopes of a call-up in white-ball cricket.

"The landscape's changed since I made my first-class debut," said Donald.

"You now have franchise cricket and these opportunities around the world to play in front of massive crowds on the biggest stage with the best players and that's a massive draw.

"Any county cricketer who comes through the system says Test cricket is the pinnacle and wanting to get a cap for England is definitely up there.

"I'm not sure I could sit here with a straight face and say I'm probably in the mix to do it in red ball.

"However this [Hundred] platform, and certainly white-ball cricket, I'm excited to see where it takes me."

After The Hundred Donald will play in a 10-over league in Canada after being involved in that format in Abu Dhabi last year.

He hopes to be involved in lucrative 20-over tournaments in UAE, Australia, South Africa and Pakistan, while the Indian Premier League (IPL) is the holy grail for franchise cricketers.

"I've always felt I've had an ability to do it at franchise level and levels above, and it's nice to feel I'm showing that now," said Donald.

"Hopefully a few doors will start to open, certainly on the franchise circuit, and then you never know with the England white ball stuff.

"All I can do is keep knocking at the door and, most importantly, performing on every stage and in every opportunity I get."

Soaring heat, falling crowds - The Hundred's peculiar summer

Given his qualities, it is no surprise Donald is a big supporter of The Hundred concept which has divided cricket fans.

"It is safe to say the standard has gone up this year, especially with the overseas players we have," said Donald.

"Guys who play in leagues around the world can't speak highly enough of The Hundred.

"You're playing with the best players in the world in front of massive crowds on TV.

"As a professional sportsman, it feels like the pinnacle right now in terms of English T20, or close to T20."

Donald also believes it has succeeded off the field.

"The Hundred has achieved a lot of what it's set out to be," he said.

"It's been obvious to see how many families and kids are in grounds throughout the school holidays.

"The product is great entertainment, although it's not perfect."

Donald hopes The Hundred can continue to co-exist alongside the T20 Blast and the 50-over One Day Cup.

"The Hundred is here to stay and hopefully supporting the county game," he said.

"While the Blast has probably had a little bit of heat over the last few years, it's a great competition with good overseas players and teams.

"It's a good proving ground, a great product itself which is well followed and well organised.

"The Hundred is a separate entity but the Blast and Metro-Bank [One Day Cup] competitions are good and county cricket is brilliant.

"There is a good will there where The Hundred can coexist and benefit the other domestic tournaments."

One thing Donald will be doing on Sunday is committing to his running between the wickets.

Earlier this month, he was in supreme form with 23 from 10 balls when he was inexplicably run out against MI London after failing to ground his bat.

"I pride myself as a relatively switched-on bloke, so to have done that has hurt my ego," said Donald, who was relieved the Rockets won by six wickets.

"This is probably a good place to get on record my apology.

"Not only do I apologise to Pete Moores and Sam Billings (Trent Rockets head coach and captain), I apologise to all my coaches from under-9s and all the way through, because that's the first rule, everyone knows to run your bat in.

"Doing that on television in a big game, when I was in good form, was pretty dumb and I have learned my lesson.

"I've seen a few clips of that online, it's tough to get rid of, and everyone since has been telling me not to forget to run my bat in this weekend.

"So that'll be first on my list. You might see me diving into the crease on Sunday!"

Donald will be hoping that will not be necessary at the home of cricket where he will aim to provide the Welsh firepower for Trent Rockets.

title: Mom charged with murder in baby's hot car death, sparking outrage
description: Dozens of kids die in hot cars every year. Some advocates say tough prosecutions don't protect kids from tragic accidents.
fullText:
An all-too-familiar tragedy unfolded in Georgia, leading to what advocates say is an unusually aggressive prosecution of a mother who unknowingly left her baby in a hot car where he died.

Daniel Coleman, 17 months old, was remembered at his funeral Aug. 15. He was the 17th child in the United States to die in a hot car in 2026, and at least three more have died since, according to Kids and Car Safety, an organization that tracks the deaths and advocates for children's safety in cars. An average of 40 children die this way every year in the country, according to the organization.

Georgia prosecutors have charged Deja Coleman, his mother, with second-degree murder, infuriating child safety advocates who say that hot car deaths are nearly always accidental and tragic. They stress that under the wrong circumstances, any parent could make the fatal mistake of leaving their child in a hot car.

Amber Rollins, the executive director of Kids and Car Safety, said Coleman was a "wonderful, loving mother" who, due to stress that compounded a common memory process in the brain, "lost awareness" that her baby was in the car and not at daycare where she believed he was all day.

"Locking people up and charging them criminally for a tragic accident that they couldn't see coming is just inhumane," Rollins said.

The Gwinnett County District Attorney's Office declined to comment.

Deja Coleman drove her three sons, ages 6, 4 and 1, to their daycare center the morning of July 29 from the shelter where they had been living. Then, she drove to the hospital where she worked as a certified nursing assistant. Hours later, a bystander called police to report an unresponsive baby inside a locked car.

Temperatures reached near 90 degrees in Lawrenceville, Georgia, in the Atlanta area that day, and 1-year-old baby Daniel did not survive. An hour after he was removed from the car by police officers, who had broken a window to get him out, the temperature inside the vehicle was recorded at 117 degrees, Lawrenceville Police Captain Dena Pauly said.

Coleman, 29, who police said had forgotten the baby in the car and was "devastated" when she learned what happened, was placed under arrest and charged with second-degree murder and second-degree cruelty to children.

Defense attorney Tom Ford said that Coleman was experiencing "medical grade" sleep deprivation. She and her boys were living at a protective shelter after she was allegedly abused by her husband, Ford and Rollins said. Her oldest child is autistic and nonspeaking, and needs significant attention and care, and the baby had been teething and not sleeping well.

Police said Coleman told investigators she had a habit of bringing the older two into the daycare first, then getting the baby out of the car and bringing him inside. Ford said she would sometimes bring all three in, with the baby on her hip, and other times take baby Daniel in separately.

"The older child has some medical needs that require special attention so that's why she always chose to take him in first," Pauly said.

According to Rollins, Coleman even brought Daniel's diaper bag inside. Though she intended to get Daniel out of the car and take him into daycare, at some point she lost awareness he was there and believed she already had brought him inside, Rollins and Ford said. The boys' normal daycare provider wasn't there that day, and the staff weren't as familiar with the kids, Rollins said.

Of cases where a child was unknowingly left in a car, about 41% do not lead to criminal charges against caregivers, Rollins said. About 31% of the total incidents end in convictions, and Rollins said many of those cases involve plea deals so a parent can avoid jail time or a drawn-out legal battle.

In 2026, there have been 12 cases of children who died after being unintentionally left in cars, and felony charges were brought in seven of those cases, Rollins said. More typically, charges in cases where children are unintentionally left may include involuntary homicide or neglect, she said.

Parents who have been charged with murder in hot car deaths before include a decade-old conviction of a father that was later overturned in Georgia. Additionally, an Arizona man pleaded guilty to murder after intentionally leaving his child in the car but died by suicide before he could be sentenced and a Texas woman was convicted after intentionally leaving her child in a car.

Though police said Coleman forgot Daniel in the car, Pauly said the second-degree murder charge in Georgia does not require malicious forethought and in Coleman's case it was "simply neglect." If convicted of the murder charge, Coleman would face between 10 and 30 years in prison.

Rollins called the charge "cruel and unusual."

"Prosecuting these tragedies criminally, it doesn't just work against prevention, it takes a traumatized parent and just absolutely destroys them. And on top of that, the living children in these families lose a parent after they've already lost a sibling, and that's just cruel," Rollins said of cases where children are unintentionally left.

When a child dies in a hot car, the most common reason is that they were unintentionally left there by a parent or other caregiver, according to data by Kids and Car Safety. Less commonly, children gain access to a car on their own and become trapped, or in some cases they are intentionally left.

It often goes something like this: One parent typically brings the child to school, but for some reason the other parent has to do it one day. They plan to do it on the way from home to their work, a drive they take every day. At some point, the brain's autopilot kicks in, and the parent ends up driving all the way to work without making the stop. It's not until the end of their work day that they discover their child was still in the car.

Children in hot car deaths were supposed to have been dropped off at daycare in about 45% of cases where they were unknowingly left in a car, according to Kids and Car Safety data.

David Diamond, a neuroscientist at the University of South Florida, studies what goes on in the brain when a parent forgets their child in a car. There is a competition in the brain between prospective memory, or the memory of things you are supposed to do in the future (such as drop a child off on the way to work) and the much stronger habit-based memory (such as the routine drive from home to work). Daniel said it's the mental process of driving away with a cup of soda on a car's roof.

Where are kids dying in hot cars? Data reveals when, where

A cup of soda and a child are of course not the same, Diamond said, but the brain function that causes someone to unintentionally leave their child in a car is the same.

"As they exit the car, they have no awareness that the child is in the car," Diamond said, adding that their brains can even create a "false memory" that they did indeed drop the child off.

Factors such as a change in routine, sleep deprivation or stress can cause prospective memory to fail much more easily, while habit-based memory is not affected by these, he said.

'Where is your baby?': Hot car death rocks New Jersey community

In his research, Diamond said he has spoken with people from all walks of life whose memory failures led to the tragic loss of their children.

"In an overwhelming majority of child hot car deaths, it was a loving, responsible parent that unknowingly left the child," Kids and Car Safety says on its website.

Diamond said that most people don't believe they could ever forget their child in a car, but denying the reality of the possibility actually makes people more "complacent."

"People just don't believe you can forget a child in a car, and that also leads to them being very judgmental against those who have," Diamond said.

Kids and Car Safety recommends taking some of the following steps to prevent a hot car tragedy:

Place your child's diaper bag or another object like a stuffed animal in the front passenger seat as a visual reminder that the child is in the car with you.

Get into the habit of opening the back door every time you park to make sure a child isn't left behind, even if you are alone. To enforce the habit, place an item you will need to start your day like your cellphone, employee badge or purse in the back seat.

Ask your childcare provider to call you right away if your child doesn't arrive as scheduled.

Communicate clearly with others who are getting each child in and out of the car.

Advocates are also pushing for lawmakers to mandate that car manufacturers include technology in cars that will alert when someone is left behind. Another law Kids and Car Safety supports is mandating that childcare providers contact parents if children do not show up as scheduled. New Jersey is the only state with such a law, Rollins said.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Mom charged with murder in baby's hot car death, sparking outrage

title: Alaska runner hospitalized after using bear spray to fight off brown bear on Alaska trail
description: A runner on Anchorage's Wolverine Bowl trail used bear spray to fend off a brown bear and was hospitalized, marking the second attack in the area in weeks.
fullText:
A runner was hospitalized in Alaska after fending off a bear attack in Anchorage this week.

The woman, who was running by herself at Prospect Heights' Wolverine Bowl trail, was able to get away from the brown bear by using her bear spray, according to the Alaska Department of Fish and Game.

She was taken to a local hospital for treatment.

Bear Attack In Yellowstone National Park Leaves 2 Hikers Injured

Biologists went to the site of the attack and collected samples but no bears were seen.

The department said anyone who sees a bear or another wild animal acting aggressively or unusually should report it.

Warning signs have been posted at the Prospect Heights trailhead, the departmet said, adding that hikers should stay off closed trails.

"Thick, dense summer foliage can block sightlines, making surprise encounters more likely," the department said. "Choose hiking routes with good visibility and away from known attractants, like salmon-bearing streams."

When hiking in bear country, people should carry a deterrent such as bear spray or a firearm, stay in groups, make noise to avoid surprising a bear, stay alert for signs of bears, don't approach bears and keep pets on a leash.

Woman Attacked By Brown Bear While Hiking With Friend And 3 Dogs Near Alaska State Park

"If you surprise a bear, especially one with cubs or on a food cache, it may react in a threatened or defensive manner," the department said. "The bear may be agitated and may huff, stomp, make a popping sound with its teeth, salivate or lay its ears back against its head and charge."

They urged staying calm, standing your ground, readying deterrent, staying in a group and talking calmly. Never run.

"If the bear is stationary, move away slowly while keeping your eyes on the bear," the department said. "If the bear starts to move toward you or charges, stop and stand your ground. Let the bear know you are not a threat. Behaving calmly, moving slowly, and speaking in a low calm voice will help de-escalate the situation. If the bear continues to approach, use your deterrent when the bear is within range."

Woman Stalked By Charging Bear On Morning Dog Walk Captures Terrifying Encounter On Camera

The attack comes less than a month after another woman was mauled by a bear in Anchorage.

The July victim was walking with a friend and her three dogs in the Bear Valley residential neighborhood, adjacent to Chugach State Park in south Anchorage, when the bear approached.

Officials said the hikers were on an unofficial, user-made trail that climbs a steep hillside in a zigzag pattern. The area was heavily overgrown with dense vegetation, which created poor visibility and increased the risk of surprising wildlife, the department said.

"The bear came out of the dense alders, made brief contact with one of the hikers, and left the scene," the department added.

The woman suffered non-life-threatening injuries and was expected to recover.

title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row, found dead
description: His family said it was "in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son" after the academic was found dead in London on Friday.
fullText:
Jason Arday, the former University of Cambridge professor at the centre of a plagiarism row, has been found dead.

Emergency services said a man was found "unresponsive" at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday afternoon.

Arday resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week after allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. He had denied the claims.

Arday's family said in a statement that they were "in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son".

They added: "The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone."

Earlier on Friday, police officers were called to an address in Battersea by the London Ambulance Service.

In a statement, the Metropolitan Police said: "At this time his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious."

Cambridge University vice-chancellor Prof Deborah Prentice said: "We are desperately saddened to hear this tragic news."

"Our heartfelt sympathies go to Jason Arday's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time," she said.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "deeply shocked and saddened" to hear about the death and she urged people to "remember there are real people with loved ones involved".

Arday, 41, had denied any plagiarism - but admitted errors in his work - and last week said the recent controversy about his work had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

The row first erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in the professor's work.

Arday said some errors in his early academic work arose because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information. Similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics, he said.

"We're talking about academia here. I didn't murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I've experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable," he told the Times newspaper earlier this month.

Arday's appointment as Cambridge's youngest ever black professor at the age of 37 in 2023 was hailed at the time as a progressive moment.

Announcing his resignation last week, Arday said the "personal cost" of the scrutiny of him had become "too great".

He said: "While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement.

"The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love."

He stressed that his resignation should not "be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me".

Cambridge initially said claims of plagiarism regarding Arday's thesis and some journal publications had been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) and the journals in question.

LJMU - which awarded Arday his PhD in 2015 - concluded that he had not plagiarised work.

Earlier this week, Cambridge announced an independent investigation into his appointment.

In a letter to university staff at the time, Prof Prentice said: "I fully understand the concerns being raised across the university and well beyond it, regarding Jason Arday's appointment and I share them...

"That investigation, as you say, should be thorough and transparent, and will be carried out independently by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge."

Cambridge celebrated Arday's appointment as a young black professor, one of a tiny and visible majority in academia. Only one per cent of professors in UK universities are black, making each appointment hugely significant.

The university will have to answer bigger questions including about its duty of care after it put him into a very prominent position.

It may also find itself the lightning rod for anger from several different quarters, including those who feel Arday was persecuted publicly and those who question whether he should ever have been appointed.

Jolyon Maugham from campaign group Good Law Project said Arday's death was "a tragedy".

"I do not understand what the public interest was in continuing to hound him after he resigned as a professor and I do not understand what risk assessments media outlets did," Maugham added.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor of Black Studies Kehinde Andrews and friend of Arday described him as "very down" after resigning from Cambridge.

"He was very upset. He felt that there was no way out. He effectively wasn't leaving the house. He had lost a lost of weight," Andrews said.

"There should be a wakeup call to just how bad black academics actually have it in academia," he added.

Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy told the programme "the idea that an academic would be dragged through this amount of media scrutiny is unheard of".

Arday originally worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at LJMU and going on to become an associate professor at Durham University and professor of sociology of education at the University of Glasgow.

Glasgow university also announced a review into Arday's previous academic work.

When news of his death emerged, the university said in a statement it was "shocked and saddened" by the death of a former colleague.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with his friends and family at this desperately sad time," it added.

Durham University, another of Arday's former employers, described him as "a kind and warm person, who actively sought to promote opportunities for PhD students".

Last weekend, Arday cancelled an event promoting his memoir.

Publisher Simon & Schuster previously said that the book, Great And Unfortunate Things, would be published in the UK on 27 August. It was released in the US earlier this week.

The book tells the story of his life from being non-verbal until the age of 11 and unable to read or write until 18, then going through a series of "improbable triumphs and heartbreaking setbacks", before being appointed professor of sociology of education at Cambridge.

title: No 10’s ads for a TikTok team show why social media is a smart career move
description:
The Guardian’s deputy editor of social platforms on the demand from high-profile people and brands for help in harnessing the power of TikTok
I didn’t want to work in social media. If you’d asked 15-year-old me my dream job, I might have said foreign correspondent, or maybe travel writer. fullText:
The Guardian’s deputy editor of social platforms on the demand from high-profile people and brands for help in harnessing the power of TikTok

I didn’t want to work in social media. If you’d asked 15-year-old me my dream job, I might have said foreign correspondent, or maybe travel writer. So you can imagine my surprise to now find myself giving these very colleagues advice on how to get the best selfie angle or write the sharpest TikTok ‘hook’.

But taking a job as the Guardian’s deputy editor of social platforms, may prove to be one of my smartest career moves if the current job market is to be believed.

You don’t need to be a digital native to have noticed the way that celebrities, brands and, yes, the prime minister, are taking their social media game seriously these days.

Westminster watchers keeping an eye on the government jobs board to get an idea of the type of people Burnham’s operation wants to recruit, noticed no less than five newly created roles for social media professionals – the most senior of them earning a touch under £70,000 per year.

Burnham’s wholesale commitment to feeding the algorithm may feel like a relative novelty on this side of the pond, but social media has been a political battleground in the US for much longer.

Early in Trump’s presidency, outgoing press secretary Karoline Leavitt could regularly be seen recapping the administration’s “successes” with the catchy “Maga minute”, and New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s masterful use of social comms is the envy of politicians the world over.

But while it’s true that the internet game requires a charismatic personality, backstage there is a squad of editors, producers and strategists making the whole thing sing. That’s where we come in.

My journey into social media began when my team at CNN took over producing for the TikTok channel in 2023. I realised that’s where audiences, including myself, really were.

If you hear the word TikTok and think it’s just dance trends and memes, think again. My job involved getting phone calls from war zones asking if I had what I needed and being sent selfies from craters. When I left earlier this year we had grown the account to almost 12 million followers.

Now mainstream media is trying to beat content creators at their own game. Oxford’s Reuters Institute this year reported that social and video networks have overtaken news websites and apps by audience share. The BBC has even hired a gen z whisperer.

As with most things in the world of social media, this change has happened rapidly, one of the consequences of that change is that there is really no such thing as a “traditional route” into the industry.

Lauren Spearman is an accidental influencer who found a TikTok following, now at 62,000, while documenting her own frustrations finding a full-time role in marketing. She now enjoys a successful freelance career consulting with the benefit of two decades of experience in social. She says she’s seen a recent shift in businesses hiring for content creators.

“Social is often infantilised but it is business critical,” Spearman said. And she’s right, the trope for years has been that interns are running the accounts of your favourite businesses, but you’re much more likely to find a savvy millennial with a marketing degree behind a brand’s X feed.

What remains to be seen is if C-suites and business leaders really understand the needs of their audiences, or those they’re hiring to cater to them. “The biggest challenge has always been educating up,” said Spearman, noting that she often sees junior roles with small salaries but large scopes and unclear remits.

“A lot of times I’ll go into businesses and there is no strategy that ladders back into what the business is doing,” she said. Let’s not forget that your social producers are often on the frontline of customer interactions and what most consumers see but often still misunderstood and sidelined.

Social media can, of course, be a place for slop; for fearmongering, for misinformation. But the vast majority of good actors are on it as a place to be entertained, informed and even exercise their civic duties.

In many ways it’s still the closest to a global town square we’ve got, fraught with algorithmic problems and regulatory loopholes as it might be. It’s time to start taking the people behind these accounts seriously.

title: Morocco arrests 111 migrants headed for Spain's Ceuta in security crackdown
description: CEUTA, Spain, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Moroccan police arrested at least 111 people on Saturday as they tried to enter Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, amid tightened security on both sides of the bo...
fullText:
CEUTA, Spain, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Moroccan police arrested at least 111 people on Saturday as they tried to enter Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, amid tightened security on both sides of the border after social media posts called for ‌another mass migrant crossing.

The attempted crossing came two weeks after more than 72,000 migrants surged into Ceuta, sparking tensions within the European Union and ‌fuelling anti-immigration rhetoric among far-right parties worldwide. At least 96 people died in the attempt to reach European soil.

A source in Morocco's Interior Ministry told Reuters those detained included 109 migrants from sub-Saharan Africa ​and two Moroccan citizens arrested in or around Fnideq, the Moroccan city opposite Ceuta.

According to Spanish news agency EFE, Moroccan police used tear gas to disperse groups of migrants gathered on hills about 3 km (1.9 miles) from the border. Reuters later saw hundreds of police officers, some in riot gear and others in plain clothes, returning from the hills outside Fnideq.

EFE and Spanish state broadcaster TVE said Morocco's Interior Ministry ordered their journalists to leave Fnideq immediately, without providing an explanation.

In Ceuta, Spanish soldiers guarded supermarkets while police ‌heavily patrolled the enclave's main streets. The city was calmer ⁠than in the days after the deadly crossing attempt on July 30.

Madrid has since installed a maritime barrier and deployed more than 500 additional police from mainland Spain, raising the total in Ceuta to more than 1,600. The Interior Ministry said the reinforcements ⁠would remain for as long as needed.

"We'll continue to deploy whatever personnel are necessary to restore normality as soon as possible and prevent events like those of July 30 from happening again," Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Thursday.

About 5,000 migrants remained in Ceuta, the minister said. Reuters saw hundreds sheltering from scorching heat under makeshift bamboo shelters on the urban ​beach ​of El Trampolin.

Grande-Marlaska said migrants who entered irregularly would not be allowed to stay in the ​enclave, travel to mainland Spain or obtain legal status, except ‌in rare cases involving extreme vulnerability. Those without a right to remain would be returned to Morocco, he said.

Earlier this week, Rabat said it was monitoring "the circulation of social media posts and messages of unknown origin" calling for a mass crossing on August 15, warning it would prosecute organisers and participants.

A Reuters witness saw reinforced security near the border, including police vans with wire shields and road checkpoints. Local media reported similar measures near Spain's other North African enclave, Melilla.

Authorities prevented several groups from boarding trains and buses to northern Morocco in cities such as Casablanca, Fez and Kenitra. However, witnesses told Reuters that some migrants from sub-Saharan Africa ‌were bypassing security checkpoints by taking mountain routes towards Fnideq.

One witness said the schools in Fnideq ​had been turned into accommodation for security forces deployed near the border.

Many of ​the young people who entered Ceuta on July 30 were fishing, swimming ​or washing at Tarajal beach on Friday.

Driss Sadik, a 22-year-old from Fez who said he swam for five hours to reach Ceuta, ‌urged others not to follow his example.

"The important thing I would ​advise people trying to cross: Don't cross ​now, my brothers. You're only going to suffer," he told Reuters.

The warning was echoed by Adil Jamil, 17.

"Those who enter aren't going to benefit from anything. There will just be more and more of us, and they won't find a solution for all," he said.

Jamil said that the mass border crossings ​were "planned by the people" who pick a date, gather ‌in Fnideq and cross together to find strength in numbers.

"If I had stayed with my parents, I would've died slowly. But if I risk ​my life, arrive and build my future ... it will be better," he said.
